messages:
alex: Heads-up: brainstorming shard-tiling + token-banking model for dedicated GPU pools. goal: keep p95 SLOs steady while avoiding big global headroom reserves.

maria: cool. do you mean shard = logical group of GPUs keyed by workload shape? or purely capacity slices?

alex: logical shards based on workload shape (seq-len, qps, model family). each shard exposes lanes (gold/silver/bronze) representing SLO tiers. admission picks lane then shard.

sam: lanes sound like nice isolation. how do tenants get bursts?

alex: burst via a token bank per tenant-per-lane. tokens accumulate when underutilized, capped by a budget. spending drains the bank. preemption order: bronze -> silver -> gold.

priya: what if workload shape drifts (short -> long seqs)? can we remap without mass evictions?

alex: yes. two mechanisms: soft-reshuffle windows that only move <X pods per window, plus runtime fallback routing to compatible shard lanes. model-variant compatibility table controls fallbacks.

maria: need an operator config example with sensible knobs.

alex: pasted quick example:

```
operatorConfig:
  shards:
    - id: shard-01
      gpu: a100-40
      capacityTiles: 64
      lanes: [gold, silver, bronze]
  rebalance:
    window: 4m
    maxPodMovesPct: 0.05
  admission:
    tokenRefillPerSec: 8
    maxBurstSecs: 20
    enableFallbackRouting: true
```

sam: nice. two follow-ups: how do we size capacityTiles (by concurrency or token throughput), and what signals avoid oscillation?

alex: capacityTiles = target concurrent sequences per GPU * safetyFactor(1.25). signals: per-shard p50/p95 latency, seq-length histogram, queued requests, token burn rate, and migration churn. use moving-average + derivative dampening.

priya: preemption opt-outs? some tenants will pay to be non-preemptible.

alex: support `no-preempt` label. operator enforces reserved minimum across shards for those tenants and flags higher billing. keep that as small tiny set to avoid fragmentation.

maria: micro-tenants problem: too many tiny reservations kills utilization. maybe a pooled micro-lane with probabilistic SLO and cheaper price?

sam: agree. pooled lane with best-effort and early-notify alerts if pooled-p95 > threshold.

jordan: what's the slow-path if admission and fallbacks fail? queue length? host fallback?

alex: fallback order: 1) try other lane-compatible shard, 2) preemptible lane in same shard, 3) short-law backoff queue (with retry header), 4) opt-in fallback to hosted API. circuit-breaker to prevent overload cascades.

maria: operationally, migration storms are scary. add jitter and progressive migration thresholds.

alex: plan: stagger moves across shards, cap moves per shard per window, and rate-limit model artifact pulls. also use leader-election per-shard to coordinate.

sam: metrics list so dashboards can be wired?

alex: propose names: shard.admissions.total, shard.lane.evictions, shard.tokens.balance, shard.p95.latency, shard.migrations.count, shard.queue.depth. alerts when shard.p95 > lane.slo*1.2 or migration.rate spikes.

priya: testing strategy? we should simulate heatmaps and run canary with pilot tenants.

alex: will add sim harness with replayable traces and a canary cluster. rollout plan: canary region -> pilot customers -> ramp. include kill-switch `legacy-global-pool: true`.

maria: billing/audit: token spends & forced preempts need audit logs for chargebacks and support tickets.

alex: yes. emit events: token.spend, preempt.forced, fallback.used. wire to billing and support.

jordan: small nit: make rebalance window configurable at per-shard level for heterogeneous infra.

alex: good idea. will add `rebalance.window` per shard.

orch-bot: checklist: sim harness added, canary namespace created, metrics dashboard template committed.

maria: next steps: alex write RFC follow-up with config primitives + sim results; priya coordinate pilot tenants; sam build dashboards.

alex: will draft RFC and share traces tomorrow morning. ping me if you want to pair on sim. :rocket:
